description:
Facts about one satellite, for "what is this satellite?" or to get its TLE.

Returns a plain-words summary, object type (payload, rocket body, debris), owner, launch date and site, re-entry date if it has come down, orbit (class, period, inclination, perigee and apogee heights in km, eccentricity), size in meters when known, its radio downlinks, and its current orbital elements as TLE lines (as OMM for catalog numbers above 99999), with their epoch and age. It takes no location and no time: for where it is use get_position, for when to see it use find_passes or find_best_pass, and for a pass's Doppler and reception use get_radio_pass. Owner, launch and type come from CelesTrak's satellite catalog and are null when it does not say; the orbit is null once it has re-entered. An unknown satellite is an error that suggests search_satellites (outside the popular list a name resolves only on an exact whole-name match). Most satellites come from SeekSat's own copy of CelesTrak's catalog, refreshed every four hours; one missing from it is looked up at CelesTrak, which can take a few seconds and is limited per hour, so prefer NORAD numbers from search_satellites.

satellite.description: NORAD catalog number (as a number or a string) or a name, e.g. 25544, "25544" or "iss".

name: get_satellite
title: Satellite details
